goal: Review the native Windows metadata inspector patch for LAB-01A.
scope: Experimental fix/lab-01a-win-native-preflight branch at base 8d99d57e09e82f5d25b55885383a0eff6a6cb0dd. Code changes are limited to the canonical preflight inspector and its Python tests. Local review only; no publication or signed AA execution grant.
plan: Review the full code and documentation diff against the recorded base SHA.
Confirm native metadata behavior in an authorized Windows QA context, including real junctions if that context permits them.
Resolve or explicitly retain blocked coverage and obtain human review before any PR preparation.
risks: Windows enumeration metadata and no-follow stat reduce exposure but do not prove that every cloud provider exposes every placeholder state or remove filesystem races.
Python 3.11 compatibility is based on API selection and synthetic tests; it was not executed under Python 3.11.
Two real-link Python tests remain skipped on the current host; the synthetic junction fixtures are not real Windows junction integration.
The general suite remains unaccepted and two process-terminating suites remain blocked by policy.
The synthetic Windows metadata fixtures use native path rules of the test host; they do not establish full Windows path semantics on Linux.

PORT-006 and PORT-007 remain open acceptance criteria: extended Windows junction paths and case-sensitive NTFS boundaries require native verification or a formally bounded support policy before merge.
validations: 2026-11-26: Python 11 total, 9 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP; exit 0 on Python 3.12.10 Windows.
2026-11-26 R3: Python 13 total, 11 PASS, 0 FAIL, 2 SKIP; RED showed one fixture AttributeError and one dependency/resolve failure before correction, then GREEN on Python 3.12.10 Windows.
2026-11-26: canonical inspector exit 0, metadataComplete true, dependencyState local in the authorized worktree.
2026-11-26: npm run typecheck exit 0 and npm run build exit 0.
2026-11-26: Guardian MCP 22 PASS, 19 in-memory and 3 real stdio with empty QA sources; exit 0.
Historical partial suite on this worktree: 611 PASS, 218 FAIL, 1 SKIP; different coverage, not rerun for this Python-only patch.
Two process-terminating suites remain BLOCKED without authorization for exact processes.
Independent reviewer report: Linux Python 3.13.5, non-root, isolated temporary directory; 13 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP, exit 0. This was not run by the local Codex runtime.
done_when: Human reviewer accepts the bounded metadata guarantees and the residual test limitations.
Private evidence is preserved by an approved transfer before worktree removal.
No commit, push, PR, merge or deploy occurs without a later human decision.

incidents.cause: resolve and link checks preceded reparse tag rejection.

incidents.symptom: RECALL_ON_OPEN is observable only in directory enumeration metadata.
incidents.provenance: Microsoft documentation and R1 code review; synthetic R2 enumeration flags tested.
incidents.cause: WIP relied on lstat for an enumeration-only signal.
incidents.resolution: Use os.scandir and DirEntry.stat(follow_symlinks=False) on Windows; missing required attributes block.
incidents.verification: PASS synthetic flags and native preflight; exhaustive provider coverage UNKNOWN.
incidents.residualRisk: scandir alone does not certify every cloud provider or remove races.
incidents.nextAction: Document bounded guarantee and test with approved native placeholders if available.

incidents.symptom: Real Windows link tests require unavailable symlink privilege.
incidents.provenance: Runtime: 2 SKIP; synthetic junction internal, external and broken cases pass.
incidents.cause: Host privilege restriction for symlink fixture creation.
incidents.resolution: Retain justified skips and add synthetic no-follow fixtures.
incidents.verification: R2 9 PASS, 2 SKIP; R3 11 PASS, 2 SKIP on Python 3.12 Windows; no real junction integration.
incidents.nextAction: Run real-link integration only in a later authorized environment.

incidents.symptom: Synthetic Windows fixture read native st_file_attributes eagerly even when a flag override existed.
incidents.provenance: Operator reported Linux AttributeError; runtime R3 RED reproduced AttributeError using a stat object with only st_mode.
incidents.cause: flags.get(path, original.st_file_attributes) evaluates its default argument before lookup; root fallback and tag constants also depended on host metadata.
incidents.resolution: Fixtures now supply synthetic Windows attributes and tags for entries and root, and patch tag constants only within the simulated context.
incidents.verification: R3 GREEN on Windows Python 3.12; Linux runtime execution NOT_RUN.
incidents.residualRisk: Synthetic sys.platform does not emulate Linux or Windows path semantics across hosts.
incidents.nextAction: Run the Python tests on a real authorized Linux host before cross-platform acceptance.

incidents.symptom: An external link elsewhere in the tree left dependencyState missing and freeBytes zero despite local node_modules.
incidents.provenance: R2 code inspection shows the final classification guard; R3 RED junction fixture failed while resolving ordinary node_modules; original real-link test was SKIP on this host.
incidents.cause: Final dependency and disk classification was gated on absence of externalLinks, datalessFiles and metadata errors.
incidents.resolution: Classify node_modules during safe entry inspection and calculate disk capacity after root verification, independently of unrelated unsafe entries.
incidents.verification: R3 GREEN targeted synthetic external-link and offline-placeholder cases; unsafe entries still block the preflight exit.
incidents.residualRisk: Real symlink and junction integration remains unverified; races remain possible.
incidents.nextAction: Review the candidate and run real-link tests only in an authorized capable environment.

incidents.symptom: A legitimate Windows junction may be reported outside the workspace when os.readlink returns an extended-path prefix.
incidents.provenance: External reviewer report supplied by the operator: an isolated PureWindowsPath.is_relative_to comparison returned false for an extended path versus a normal path. No real Windows junction integration was run.
incidents.cause: Potential representation mismatch between extended and normal Windows paths; application-level failure not reproduced.
incidents.resolution: OPEN; no code change in this reconciliation.
incidents.verification: Hypothesis supported by the reviewer-supplied path comparison; native junction behavior UNKNOWN.
incidents.residualRisk: False blocking of a legitimate internal junction.
incidents.nextAction: Before merge, verify real Windows junctions and resolve the classification or formally delimit support.

incidents.symptom: Case-sensitive NTFS directory boundaries may be classified incorrectly by lexical workspace membership checks.
incidents.provenance: External reviewer report supplied by the operator: isolated PureWindowsPath.is_relative_to comparison treated paths differing only by case as equivalent. No workspace escape was reproduced.
incidents.cause: Potential mismatch between Python path comparison and per-directory NTFS case sensitivity; exploitability UNKNOWN.
incidents.resolution: OPEN; no code change in this reconciliation.
incidents.verification: Reviewer-supplied isolated comparison only; real vulnerability NOT_REPRODUCED.
incidents.residualRisk: Incorrect workspace membership classification in a case-sensitive directory.
incidents.nextAction: Before merge, test the boundary on an authorized case-sensitive NTFS directory and fix or formally delimit support.
